title: Sink-kind vocabulary contract
description: Canonical structured record pinning the three names a sink's 'kind' carries across Herald layers, and the rule that says which name is canonical at each boundary. A sink's identity crosses several boundaries — the catalog endpoint, the instance store, the bootstrap JSON, the Build() dispatch, the provider-resolution call, and the sink implementation itself. Each boundary speaks one of three vocabularies: catalog kind (the wire/storage name), OSS kind (the QuickLogBuilder call-site name), or provider class (implementation-internal). This record is the single source of truth so the divergence Jared and Richard fixed during the sink-kind unification work cannot regrow. The doc-site contract page, any future API reference, and the FakeServer/OSS xmldoc cross-references all read from this record. Edit once; every render regenerates.

surface.description: URL-safe slug for this contract record. Lowercase alphanumerics and hyphens. Used as the file slug and the deep-link namespace.

version.description: ISO-8601 date of the record's last substantive update (YYYY-MM-DD). Bumped any time the rule, the layer table, or a vocabulary changes.

last_reviewed.description: ISO-8601 date the record was last verified against the live code (YYYY-MM-DD). A stale review date means the record is suspect until re-checked against the source files in 'source_files'.

title.description: Human-readable title rendered on the page hero.

ratified_by.description: Who ratified the canonical rule (e.g. 'Richard, architecture-designer'). Optional, but recorded when the rule was the output of an architectural decision.

source_files.description: The code files this record was verified against. The renderer lists these so the next reader can re-check the record against the live code.

role.description: What this file proves about the contract (e.g. 'Build() dispatch switch — matches catalog kind').

vocabularies.description: The three names a sink's kind can take. Each is named once here and referenced by id from the layer table.

id.description: Stable identifier the layer rows reference.

name.description: The display name of the vocabulary (e.g. 'catalog kind').

definition.description: One-sentence definition of what this vocabulary is and where it is allowed to appear.

may_appear_on_wire.description: True when this vocabulary is allowed in any stored or transmitted field. The whole point of the contract: only catalog kind is true.

layers.description: Each boundary a sink identity crosses, and which vocabulary it speaks. This is the layer-to-vocabulary mapping that is the heart of the record.

layer.description: The boundary or component (e.g. 'Catalog endpoint', 'Bootstrap JSON').

symbol.description: The concrete code symbol or field at this layer (e.g. 'SinkCatalogEntry.KindKey', 'sinks[].kind').

speaks.description: Which vocabulary id this layer uses.

example.description: A concrete example value at this layer (e.g. 'herald.json-file', 'json_file', 'WriterLogger (never surfaced)').

rule.description: The canonical rule, broken into the statement plus the three vocabulary dispositions.

statement.description: The one-paragraph rule, written at a high-school reading level.

canonical.description: Where the catalog/wire kind is canonical.

scoped.description: Where the OSS kind is allowed, and only there.

forbidden.description: Where the provider class must never appear.

consequence.description: The concrete consequence of getting the rule wrong — why this is a real bug, not a style preference.

detail.description: The cause-and-effect walk: stored provider class -> dispatch miss -> silent sink drop.

do_dont.description: The one-line do/don't a future contributor reads first.

analogy.description: The callout analogy that anchors the catalog-kind-vs-provider-class distinction. Rendered as a quick-picture callout box.
